Not in GUI, but in CLI

SATOM shows every field and object a device has on its exact build; whatever the Fortinet GUI does not draw is listed under "Not in GUI, but in CLI" — per object in every editor, and per device on one page with the objects the GUI never reads and their rows.

👤 ForOperatorAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view protection.view appliances.edit network.edit protection.edit
📍 WhereEvery object editor and product view (section "Not in GUI, but in CLI"); per device at Appliances → (device) → Not in GUI, but in CLI (URL /appliances/<id>/not-in-gui), also the last entry of the FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator and FortiAnalyzer device menus

What is it?#

SATOM follows one rule for every product: it shows every field a device has on its exact firmware build. A field or object the Fortinet GUI does not show is never dropped and never merged into another group. It goes to a section titled Not in GUI, but in CLI, which says how SATOM writes each field. The per-device page of the same name collects everything one device has outside its GUI, including whole objects that no page of the device's GUI reads.

What does it do?#

  • Ends every object editor and product view with a collapsed section Not in GUI, but in CLI (n). The section is always drawn; when it is empty it says why (Every field this object has on this build is in the Fortinet GUI., or the page's GUI layout has not been measured yet).
  • Marks each field with the channel SATOM writes it by:
Badge Meaning
REST The REST API serves the field. A normal save writes it.
CLI This build does not serve the field over REST. SATOM writes it over SSH with the CLI writer.
unverified on this build No source measured the field on this build. It is shown, never hidden, and not written until a channel is measured.

  • On a FortiADC, REST spells many fields differently from the CLI (direct_route_ip / direct-route-ip, mkey / name, and renames such as pool / load-balance-pool). A field both spellings name is the same field and stays in its GUI group under its REST name. Outright renames are measured per build (7.6.7 and 8.0.4) and shown as one field under the REST name; on a build that was not measured, or for a field no measured rename covers, a CLI field REST does not name is shown as unverified on this build, not as CLI. CLI is used only for objects REST answers 404 for on the device's build.

  • Decides "not in the GUI" from two kinds of evidence: the API library of the device's exact build (a field the CLI has and REST does not is never in the GUI) and, where one was measured, the page's GUI layout (a REST field the layout does not place is not in the GUI either).

  • Offers one page per device that lists, in one place, every object and field the device's build has outside the GUI.

Requirements#

  • The appliance's running build must be known. Without it the page says The running build of this appliance is unknown: run a firmware check so SATOM can name the fields it has outside the GUI.
  • GUI layouts and API-library evidence for the build, which arrive with the knowledge packs. Without a measured layout for a product, every field the REST API returns stays in the object views and nothing is hidden.
  • For writing CLI fields: SSH access to the device with the appliance credentials.

Permissions#

Action Permission
Open the per-device page, Read values over CLI appliances.view
See the rows of the objects the device's GUI does not draw, Open its page protection.view
Preview CLI change and Apply Any key that grants configuration writes (legacy config_write), for example appliances.edit, network.edit or protection.edit

🔑Permission — Without the permission

The menu entry is not drawn for a user who may not open the page. Without protection.view the list of objects the GUI does not draw is shown without their rows. Without a write key, the CLI fields are listed read-only and the Preview CLI change and Apply buttons are not rendered.

How to use#

Open the per-device page#

  1. Open the device in Appliances, or select it in its product ADOM.
  2. Click Not in GUI, but in CLI. On a FortiADC, FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator or FortiAnalyzer it is an entry of the device's own menu in the sidebar, after the menu's pages. Every "Not in GUI, but in CLI" section also links to it as Everything this device has outside the GUI →.

The page lists, depending on the product and the build:

Card What it lists
Layout-measured pages Per page whose GUI layout was measured: the REST fields the Fortinet GUI does not show.
Objects the device's GUI does not draw Whole objects the device serves over REST that no page of its own GUI reads on this build, each with its rows.
Objects only the CLI serves Whole objects REST does not have at all (for example FortiAuthenticator system/dns).
CLI-only fields of objects the REST API serves Per object, the fields only the CLI has.

The same inventory, without field values and the editor, is on the operator console: sudo satom get device not-in-gui <device> [--endpoint <key or cli path>] (see CLI). It reads the API library and the measured layouts; the device is not contacted.

Read the objects the GUI does not draw#

  1. On the per-device page, find Objects the device's GUI does not draw.
  2. Each object shows its label, its REST path with a REST badge and the menu group it belongs to. Its rows are read from the device when the page opens (Reading rows…), read only. A settings object is shown as Field / Value; a table shows the columns of the page SATOM draws it on, or every field when that page has none.
  3. Click Open its page to go to the page SATOM draws the object on. An object with no page says no measured page of this build reads it: this list is where SATOM shows it.

The list is derived from the GUI layouts of the device's build and from the endpoint registry; it is never a fixed list. An object the build answers 404 for is not listed. On a lab FortiADC 7.6.7 it holds 46 objects: VDOM and VDOM links, per-VDOM syslog and FortiAnalyzer, DNS, ISP provinces, connection pool, alert targets and others, plus Auto Backup, which the build serves but no measured page reads (its GUI tab is an action).

On a FortiAnalyzer 7.6.7 build 3737 the device menu's Not in GUI, but in CLI group holds 43 pages, one per CLI object the FortiAnalyzer GUI never edits (for example system ha, system ntp, system sql, fmupdate service). Each page reads its /cli/global/... object live over JSON-RPC and is writable like a configuration page: a dry run shows the exact JSON-RPC request, Apply sends it to the object's own URL and reads the object back to verify it. On FortiAnalyzer the JSON-RPC URL is the CLI path, so no field goes over SSH. See FortiAnalyzer workspace.

Change a CLI-only field#

  1. In a Not in GUI, but in CLI section (or on the per-device page), name the row in Row (and its parent in Row of, for a nested table).
  2. Click Read values over CLI. SATOM reads the current values over a read-only SSH session (show full-configuration). Secrets are never returned; their input says secret — not shown.
  3. Change the values and click Preview CLI change to see the script.
  4. Click Apply. The CLI writer runs the script and reads the object back in a fresh session.

In an editor you can write to, the section's fields are part of the form and the normal save sends them: REST fields over REST, CLI fields through the CLI writer. On a Create New form a CLI-only field says CLI-only on this build: set it once the object exists.

Example#

🧪Example — Find the VDOM settings of a FortiADC

An operator looks for the per-VDOM syslog settings of adc-01 and cannot find them in the device's GUI. In SATOM, FortiADC → Not in GUI, but in CLI lists the per-VDOM syslog object under Objects the device's GUI does not draw, with its rows read from the device. Open its page opens the page SATOM draws for it.

Result#

  • Opening the page and reading rows change nothing on the device.
  • Apply writes the CLI-only fields and records appliance.not_in_gui.save in the Audit log. A preview is not audited.

Troubleshooting#

"nothing was sent: …"#

Possible causes - The write named a field the build serves over REST (served by the REST API on this build: edit it in the object's own form, not by CLI) or a field no source measured on this build.

Solution 1. Edit REST fields in the object's own form. 2. Leave unverified fields alone until the build is measured.

Verification — Preview CLI change shows the script without an error.

A write with any refused field sends nothing, so a half-applied change cannot happen.

"Not read: …" under an object#

Possible causes - The device refused or did not answer the read of that object.

Solution 1. Check the appliance with Test Connection and reload the page.

Verification — the object shows its rows or No rows on the device.

The page says the CLI tree is not measured#

Possible causes - The API library has no CLI tree for this build, so CLI-only fields cannot be named yet.

Solution 1. Import a knowledge pack that covers the build.

Verification — the note disappears and the CLI cards fill in.

"SATOM has no CLI writer for …"#

Possible causes - The product has no CLI writer, or the API library does not name the CLI path of the object on this build.

Solution — the fields are listed for reference only; change them on the device's own CLI.

Advanced#

Advanced Where the lists come from
  • Objects the device's GUI does not draw are the views of every page the knowledge pack marks gui_absent for the device's firmware: the GUI crawl opened every menu entry and recorded every read, and no entry read these objects. SATOM draws them from the device's schema. Their section in an editor says that no page of the device's GUI reads the object.
  • On FortiADC only, the list also holds the registry entities the build serves that no measured page reads at all. A child table belongs to its parent's page and is not listed. On FortiWeb, FortiGate and FortiAuthenticator a collection without a page is treated as a gap of the crawl, not as an absence, so it is not listed.
  • Rows are read one object at a time through the product's own adapter (FortiADC: GET /api/<entity>), with secret fields removed. The rows route answers only for an object of the list; it never reads an arbitrary path.
  • When the CLI dialect of a product has not been verified on a device yet, a note asks you to read the previewed script before you apply.
